inferences.statement: Frontend and frontend-proxy errors are propagated from checkout's failing cart calls, so frontend is a symptom and not the origin.
The cart pod restart at 15:53:56 is the most likely point where cart stopped serving on 8080, since no listening message follows it.

root_causes.cause: Cart stopped accepting connections on port 8080 after its pod restart at 15:53:56; checkout and frontend get ECONNREFUSED on 10.96.223.207:8080. The likely cause is a changed port or config in the restarted pod, not a flag.

Checkout's errors began at 15:44 with a revision that moved the payment client to port 9999, which may have contributed. Checkout's config was later reverted (PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080). This is a secondary candidate and does not explain the cart refusals.

diagnosis.summary: The frontend ErrorBudgetBurn is a downstream symptom. Checkout's calls to cart (GetCart/AddItem, 10.96.223.207:8080) are refused with ECONNREFUSED, which surfaces as 500s in frontend and frontend-proxy. Cart's pod was restarted at 15:53:56 ('definition changed'), and its logs show no 'listening' line after the 15:31:30 startup, so cart may not be listening on 8080 since the restart. Checkout's own logs are clean, all feature flags are off, and checkout's PAYMENT_ADDR change (9999 to 8080) is not the cause of the cart errors. Confidence is moderate because checkout's error onset (15:44) predates the cart restart, and cart's server-span counters continue to rise after 15:53, which does not fit a fully dead listener.

actions.reason: Cart's container was restarted at 15:53:56 and logs show no listening line after it, while checkout gets ECONNREFUSED on cart:8080. Cart has one unchanged revision, so a rollback is not possible; a rolling restart re-runs the process to restore the listener.

alternatives.why_not: Cart has a single revision (ev_fbdd8a45ce5b77b7) unchanged since 15:30, so there is no earlier release to return to and no bad release is shown for cart.
The failure is connection refused on a listener, not a capacity shortfall, so more replicas would not restore the port.
Doing nothing leaves checkout and frontend failing; the restart is low-risk and reversible, so it is worth proposing despite moderate confidence.

plan.summary: Proposes a rolling restart of cart, the service where the diagnosis locates the origin: after the 15:53:56 pod restart, cart logs show no listening line and checkout gets ECONNREFUSED on cart:8080, which frontend and frontend-proxy surface as 500s. Expected outcome if correct: cart listens on 8080 again and checkout and frontend error ratios fall back toward zero.

inferences.statement: Frontend-proxy's error burn is caused by cart being unreachable, which propagates through checkout and frontend. Frontend-proxy is the alerting service but not the root cause.

root_causes.cause: cart's pod was killed and restarted at 15:53:56 and did not come back serving: no server traffic and no logs since, while checkout and frontend see connection refused to cart's address. Most likely the restarted container failed to start or is not ready. The cause of the 'definition changed' restart is unknown: the deployment shows no new revision.

diagnosis.summary: frontend-proxy's fast burn is downstream. Cart's only pod was killed at 15:53:56 ('definition changed, will be restarted'). After that, cart's server spans and logs stop. Checkout and frontend then get gRPC UNAVAILABLE 'connection refused' to 10.96.223.207:8080 (cart's address), and those errors propagate to frontend and frontend-proxy. Checkout's error ratio rose from about 15:44, before frontend-proxy's, which fits the call chain. No feature flags are on, and the cart deployment has only revision 1 (15:30:15), so the restart did not come from a new rollout.

actions.reason: Cart's only pod was killed at 15:53:56 for a 'definition changed' drift, and its replacement ran the pause image, so nothing serves port 8080. A rolling restart recreates the pod from the Deployment template, which has no new revision.

alternatives.why_not: Cart has only revision 1, created before the incident, so there is no earlier revision to return to.
Scaling does not fix a pod that is running the wrong image and not serving port 8080.
The live pod is clearly broken and a restart is low-risk, so waiting leaves checkout and frontend failing.

plan.summary: Rolling-restart cart so its pod is recreated from the Deployment template and serves port 8080 again. That should clear the connection-refused errors in checkout and frontend, and then frontend-proxy. Afterwards, confirm cart serves traffic and that the template image is the cart application image, not pause.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's ErrorBudgetBurn is caused by the cart service being down. Checkout's PlaceOrder and frontend's cart calls fail with 'connection refused' to cart's address 10.96.223.207:8080. Cart's pod was killed at 15:53:56 because its container definition changed. Cart's logs stop at that moment with a shutdown, and its server and client span rates drop to roughly zero. Cart has no revision change in rollout history, so the pod spec was altered outside a tracked rollout. All flags are off, so flagd is not the cause. Checkout's error ratio was 0.39 at 15:56 against 0.92 at its peak; it dipped to zero briefly and rose again.

actions.reason: Cart pod was altered in place at 15:53:56 and now pulls and runs gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest instead of the service image. Rollout history shows only revision 1, so the Deployment template is intact; a restart recreates the pod from it.

alternatives.why_not: No tracked revision change exists for cart (only revision 1), so there is no earlier revision to return to.
Adding replicas does not fix a pod running the wrong container; the failure is not a capacity problem.

plan.summary: Cart's pod was changed in place at 15:53:56 and is now running a pause placeholder image that does not listen on 8080, so checkout and frontend get connection refused. A rolling restart of cart recreates the pod from the unchanged revision-1 template, which should restore service. A human should also check the 15:44 dip for an earlier cart disruption.
